claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
The proposed intervention is addition of 10 at.% Al to HfMoTaTiZr.
Adding 10 at.% Al will reduce the alloy density by 5%.
Adding 10 at.% Al will lower density from 10.21 to approximately 9.7 g cm−3.
Adding 10 at.% Al will not sacrifice room-temperature mechanical properties.
Adding 10 at.% Al will not sacrifice elevated-temperature mechanical properties up to approximately 1000 °C.
Al addition will produce a low-density, high-temperature-stable phase.
The low density of Al will reduce the density of the alloy.
Formation of the proposed stable phase will maintain the alloy's high-temperature strength.
The proposed performance boundary is temperatures from room temperature through 1000 °C.
The proposed loading boundary is loading that does not exceed the alloy's yield strength.
The identity and elevated-temperature stability of the proposed low-density phase may vary and affect mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims no sacrifice of mechanical properties, but the rejection rule permits as much as a 10% reduction in yield strength at 1000 °C without falsification.

The hypothesis covers room temperature and elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C and broadly refers to mechanical properties, whereas the rejection rule addresses only density and yield strength at 1000 °C; it does not reject losses in room-temperature properties, ultimate tensile strength, or intermediate-temperature performance.
